lesson_scope: Argand diagram geometry, vector displacements, distance formulas, pure rotations by pi/2 and arbitrary angles, polygon construction (squares, parallelograms, rhombuses, equilateral triangles), collinearity and perpendicularity quotients, and circle tangent lines in the complex plane.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Distance between two points in the Argand plane.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Distance between two complex coordinates.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Pure rotation by pi/2 via multiplication by i.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Multiplication by i for rotation by 90 degrees.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Fourth vertex of a parallelogram using vector addition.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding opposite vertex in parallelogram.

hints: Use parallelogram vector relation: $z_B = z_A + z_C$.

walkthrough.text:
Apply vector relation for parallelogram $OABC$:
$$z_C = z_B - z_A = (1 + 6\mathrm{i}) - (3 + 2\mathrm{i}) = -2 + 4\mathrm{i}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Angle between two segments via argument subtraction.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding angle subtended at origin.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Showing isosceles triangle and finding perpendicular height.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving isosceles triangle and perpendicular distance.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate side lengths $PQ$ and $QR$:
$$PQ = |(4 + 6\mathrm{i}) - (1 + 2\mathrm{i})| = |3 + 4\mathrm{i}| = 5$$
$$QR = |(7 + 2\mathrm{i}) - (4 + 6\mathrm{i})| = |3 - 4\mathrm{i}| = 5$$
$$\text{Since } PQ = QR = 5, \triangle PQR \text{ is isosceles.}$$

Calculate the perpendicular height:
$$\text{Midpoint of base } PR \text{ is } z_M = \frac{(1 + 2\mathrm{i}) + (7 + 2\mathrm{i})}{2} = 4 + 2\mathrm{i}$$
$$\text{Height } = |z_Q - z_M| = |(4 + 6\mathrm{i}) - (4 + 2\mathrm{i})| = |4\mathrm{i}| = 4$$

ai_rubric.observable: Concludes $PQ = QR = 5$ so $\triangle PQR$ is isosceles.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Constructing equilateral triangle vertex via complex rotation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Equilateral triangle construction using polar rotation.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Proving isosceles right-angled triangle and computing area.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Multiplication by i as 90-degree rotation.

hints: Recognise multiplication by $\mathrm{i}$ as anticlockwise rotation by $\frac{\pi}{2}$.

walkthrough.text:
Compute $z\omega$ in Cartesian form:
$$z\omega = \mathrm{i}(-2 + 4\mathrm{i}) = -2\mathrm{i} + 4\mathrm{i}^2 = -4 - 2\mathrm{i}$$
$$\text{Transformation: anticlockwise rotation through } \frac{\pi}{2} \text{ about the origin.}$$

ai_rubric.observable: States anticlockwise rotation of $\frac{\pi}{2}$ (or $90^\circ$) about origin.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving isosceles right-angled triangle and area.

walkthrough.text:
Show side lengths are equal:
$$|OA| = |-2 + 4\mathrm{i}| = \sqrt{4 + 16} = \sqrt{20}$$
$$|OB| = |-4 - 2\mathrm{i}| = \sqrt{16 + 4} = \sqrt{20}$$
$$\angle AOB = \arg(\mathrm{i}) = \frac{\pi}{2}$$
$$\text{Hence } \triangle OAB \text{ is an isosceles right-angled triangle.}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Proving collinearity and perpendicularity via complex quotients.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving collinearity using real quotient.

hints: Since $\frac{3}{2} \in \mathbb{R}$, the points are collinear, and $AB : BC = 2 : 1$.

walkthrough.text:
Evaluate quotient to show collinearity:
$$\frac{z_C - z_A}{z_B - z_A} = \frac{3(1 + 2\mathrm{i})}{2(1 + 2\mathrm{i})} = \frac{3}{2}$$
$$\text{Since } \frac{3}{2} \in \mathbb{R}, A, B, C \text{ are collinear with } AB : BC = 2 : 1.$$

ai_rubric.observable: Evaluates quotient as $\frac{3}{2} \in \mathbb{R}$ to prove collinearity.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving perpendicularity using purely imaginary quotient.

hints: Since the quotient is purely imaginary, $AD \perp AC$.

walkthrough.text:
Evaluate the quotient:
$$\frac{z_D - z_A}{z_C - z_A} = \frac{-2 + \mathrm{i}}{3(1 + 2\mathrm{i})} = \frac{(-2 + \mathrm{i})(1 - 2\mathrm{i})}{3(5)} = \frac{5\mathrm{i}}{15} = \frac{1}{3}\mathrm{i}$$
$$\text{Since } \frac{1}{3}\mathrm{i} \in \mathrm{i}\mathbb{R}, AD \perp AC.$$

ai_rubric.observable: Deduces that because quotient is purely imaginary, $AD \perp AC$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Equilateral triangle analysis and geometric rotation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding moduli and subtended angle.
Proving equilateral triangle and rotating to find fourth vertex.

hints: Observe that $|OP| = |OQ| = 4$ and $\angle POQ = \frac{\pi}{3} \implies \triangle OPQ$ is equilateral.

walkthrough.text:
Deduce $\triangle OPQ$ is equilateral:
$$\text{Since } |OP| = |OQ| = 4 \text{ and } \angle POQ = \frac{\pi}{3}, \triangle OPQ \text{ is equilateral.}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Circle locus equation and perpendicular tangent line vector.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding circle equation passing through origin.
Finding tangent vector and tangent line equation.

hints: Gradient of tangent is $m = -\frac{3}{4}$, giving line $3x + 4y = 0$.

walkthrough.text:
Find tangent vector at origin perpendicular to $\vec{OC} = 6 + 8\mathrm{i}$:
$$\vec{T} = \mathrm{i}(6 + 8\mathrm{i}) = -8 + 6\mathrm{i}$$

Find Cartesian tangent line equation:
$$\text{Gradient of } OC = \frac{8}{6} = \frac{4}{3} \implies m = -\frac{3}{4}$$
$$y = -\frac{3}{4}x \implies 3x + 4y = 0$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Rotation about non-origin centre and complete square construction.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Rotation about arbitrary complex centre.

walkthrough.text:
Compute relative displacement from centre $A$:
$$z_P - z_A = (5 + 3\mathrm{i}) - (2 + \mathrm{i}) = 3 + 2\mathrm{i}$$

Rotate by $\frac{\pi}{2}$ and translate back:
$$z_Q - z_A = \mathrm{i}(3 + 2\mathrm{i}) = -2 + 3\mathrm{i}$$
$$z_Q = (2 + \mathrm{i}) + (-2 + 3\mathrm{i}) = 4\mathrm{i}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding opposite vertex and area of constructed square.

hints: Side length squared is $3^2 + 2^2 = 13$, so Area $= 13$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate opposite vertex $z_R$:
$$z_R = z_A + (z_P - z_A) + (z_Q - z_A) = (2 + \mathrm{i}) + (1 + 5\mathrm{i}) = 3 + 6\mathrm{i}$$

Calculate area of square:
$$\text{Side length } s = |3 + 2\mathrm{i}| = \sqrt{3^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{13}$$
$$\text{Area} = s^2 = 13$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Triangle distance, cosine rule verification, and dual area calculation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding displacement distance and non-right-angled observation.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate displacement vector and distance:
$$z_B - z_A = (3 + 3\sqrt{3}\,\mathrm{i}) - 2 = 1 + 3\sqrt{3}\,\mathrm{i}$$
$$AB = \sqrt{1^2 + (3\sqrt{3})^2} = \sqrt{1 + 27} = \sqrt{28} = 2\sqrt{7}$$

Check angle at origin:
$$\angle AOB = \arg(z_B) - \arg(z_A) = \frac{\pi}{3} - 0 = \frac{\pi}{3} \neq \frac{\pi}{2}$$
$$\text{Hence } \triangle OAB \text{ is not right-angled at } O.$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Verifying triangle side length using cosine rule.

walkthrough.text:
Apply the cosine rule to $\triangle OAB$ with sides $OA = 2, OB = 6$ and angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$:
$$AB^2 = 2^2 + 6^2 - 2(2)(6)\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = 4 + 36 - 24\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 28$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Calculating exact area using trigonometric and base-height methods.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate area using Cartesian base and height:
$$\text{Base} = OA = 2, \quad \text{Height} = \operatorname{Im}(z_B) = 3\sqrt{3}$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 3\sqrt{3} = 3\sqrt{3}$$
$$\text{Both calculations give identical area } 3\sqrt{3}.$$
